scope: 23 verified major scheduled passenger airlines in Nigeria (past and present): 11 active scheduled passenger carriers, 2 carriers with suspended scheduled operations as of October 2026, and 10 landmark historical scheduled airlines from 1958 to 2019.
notes: Manually curated Nigerian civil aviation reference verified against Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) Air Operator Certificate (AOC) and regulatory notices, International Air Transport Association (IATA) member records, ICAO Doc 8585 designator records, Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) hub records, and official airline publications. Excludes private business-jet charter-only operators, offshore helicopter-only contractors, cargo-only carriers, and short-lived single-aircraft operators without verifiable scheduled passenger histories. NaijaCheck does not sell tickets, quote airfares, or publish flight timetables.

airlines.name: Air Peace
airlines.serviceScope: Nigeria's largest private scheduled carrier by fleet and passenger volume, operating domestic trunk and secondary routes, West African regional services, and intercontinental flights including London.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA Air Operator Certificate (AOC) holder and IATA member airline (accounting code 710). Founded by Allen Onyema in 2013, Air Peace commenced commercial passenger operations in October 2014 from Murtala Muhammed Airport in Lagos.

airlines.serviceScope: State-backed scheduled domestic and West African regional passenger carrier operating Airbus A220 and Bombardier CRJ900 jets out of Victor Attah International Airport in Uyo.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder and IATA member airline (accounting code 704), wholly owned by the Akwa Ibom State Government. Commenced commercial passenger flights on 7 June 2019 and expanded into regional West African service including Accra.

airlines.name: United Nigeria Airlines
airlines.serviceScope: Privately owned Nigerian scheduled passenger carrier connecting Enugu, Abuja, Lagos, Port Harcourt, Owerri, Asaba, Warri, Sokoto, Kano, and regional West African gateways.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder and IOSA-certified Nigerian carrier. Incorporated in 2020 by Obiora Okonkwo, granted its NCAA AOC on 1 February 2021, and commenced commercial passenger flights on 12 February 2021 between Lagos and Enugu.

airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder founded in 2018 by Kunle Soname. Commenced scheduled commercial passenger flights on 10 October 2022. Holds the active 2-character IATA designator VK (reassigned by IATA years after Air Nigeria ceased operations in 2012) alongside ICAO code FVJ.

airlines.name: Overland Airways
airlines.serviceScope: Long-running Nigerian regional and hinterland scheduled carrier linking Abuja and Lagos with secondary state capitals including Ilorin, Akure, Ibadan, Jalingo, and Minna using Embraer E175 and ATR turboprop aircraft.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder, IATA member airline (accounting code 559), and IOSA-registered operator since 2015. Incorporated in September 1998 by Capt. Edward Boyo and commenced commercial operations in November 2002; its IATA designator transitioned from OJ to OF.

airlines.name: Green Africa Airways
airlines.serviceScope: Lagos-based value scheduled passenger airline operating ATR 72-600 turboprops across southern and central Nigerian routes including Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Benin City, Owerri, Akure, Ibadan, Enugu, and Ilorin.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder founded by Babawande Afolabi. Received its NCAA AOC on 9 August 2021 and operated its inaugural commercial passenger flight on 12 August 2021 from Lagos; expanded owned ATR 72-600 capacity in February 2026.

airlines.name: Arik Air
airlines.serviceScope: Scheduled domestic passenger airline operating Boeing 737 and Bombardier Q400/CRJ aircraft from Lagos and Abuja to Port Harcourt, Benin City, Warri, Asaba, and Jos.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder (IATA W3 / ICAO ARA, accounting code 725). airlines.fullLegalName: Aero Contractors Company of Nigeria Limited
airlines.serviceScope: Nigeria's oldest continuously registered aviation company, combining fixed-wing scheduled domestic passenger services, rotary-wing offshore oil-and-gas support, and certified aircraft maintenance (MRO) in Lagos.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder and approved Maintenance Organisation. Formed in 1959 (incorporated in Nigeria in 1960), majority-owned (60%) by the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) since financial restructuring in 2013, and active on scheduled domestic routes.

airlines.name: Max Air
airlines.serviceScope: Kano-headquartered scheduled domestic passenger carrier and major wide-body Hajj/Umrah pilgrimage operator flying Boeing 737 and Boeing 747-400 aircraft.
airlines.statusContext: Active NCAA AOC holder founded by Alhaji Dahiru Barau Mangal (originally as Mangal Airlines in 2006, rebranded Max Air in 2008; domestic scheduled flights began in 2018). airlines.name: Dana Air
airlines.serviceScope: Private Nigerian domestic trunk carrier (part of Dana Group) that operated McDonnell Douglas MD-82/MD-83 and Boeing 737-300 aircraft on Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Owerri, and Enugu routes.
airlines.statusContext: Suspended by regulator: commenced commercial flights on 10 November 2008, but the NCAA suspended Dana Air's Air Operator Certificate effective 24 April 2024 following an MD-82 (5N-BKI) runway excursion at Lagos and ordered a comprehensive safety and financial audit. No scheduled passenger resumption had been cleared as of October 2026.

airlines.name: Azman Air
airlines.serviceScope: Kano-based domestic passenger and Hajj carrier founded by Abdulmunaf Yunusa Sarina that operated Boeing 737 Classic jets and an Airbus A340-600.
airlines.statusContext: Scheduled domestic flights suspended: incorporated in 2010 and commenced domestic passenger services in May 2014 from Kano. In August 2024, Azman Air indefinitely halted domestic passenger operations and placed staff on unpaid leave citing overseas C-check maintenance delays across its Boeing 737 fleet; active IATA designator is omitted because international profiles list IATA n/a post-suspension (historically ZQ).

airlines.name: Nigeria Airways
airlines.iataHistoricalNote: Historical IATA designator WT held 1958–2003 (subsequently reassigned globally by IATA after liquidation).
airlines.serviceScope: Nigeria's state-owned national flag carrier for 45 years, operating domestic, West African, European (London), North American (New York), and Jeddah routes with Vickers VC10, Boeing 707/737/747, McDonnell Douglas DC-10, and Airbus A310 aircraft.
airlines.statusContext: Ceased and liquidated in 2003: established on 23 August 1958 (commencing flights 1 October 1958) as WAAC Nigeria following the dissolution of the colonial West African Airways Corporation, became 100% federally owned in 1961, adopted the Nigeria Airways name and 'Skypower' elephant emblem in 1971, and closed in 2003 under heavy debt.

sources.label: Wikipedia — Nigeria Airways (WT / NGA, 1958–2003 national flag carrier)
Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) — Aviation Heritage & Hub Airports

airlines.notes: Former national flag carrier ('Skypower', WT / NGA); founded as WAAC Nigeria in 1958, renamed in 1971, liquidated in 2003.

airlines.name: Air Nigeria
airlines.iataHistoricalNote: Historical IATA designator VK held 2005–2012 (reassigned by IATA to Nigerian carrier ValueJet in the 2020s).
airlines.serviceScope: Designated post-Nigeria Airways flag carrier joint venture that operated domestic, West/Central African regional, London Heathrow/Gatwick, and Johannesburg passenger routes.
airlines.statusContext: Rebranded twice before ceasing operations on 10 September 2012: founded in 2004 by Nigerian institutional investors (51%) and Virgin Atlantic (49%) as Virgin Nigeria Airways (inaugural Lagos–London flight 28 June 2005, ICAO VGN). Following Virgin Atlantic's exit, it rebranded to Nigerian Eagle Airlines in September 2009 and Air Nigeria (ICAO ANP) in June 2010 before shutting down in September 2012.

sources.label: Wikipedia — Air Nigeria (Virgin Nigeria / Nigerian Eagle, 2004–2012)

airlines.notes: Founded as Virgin Nigeria (2004), rebranded Nigerian Eagle (2009) and Air Nigeria (2010); ceased 10 September 2012. Historical IATA VK later reassigned to ValueJet.

airlines.name: Bellview Airlines
airlines.iataHistoricalNote: Historical IATA designator B3 held 1992–2009 (subsequently reassigned by IATA to Bhutan Airlines).
airlines.serviceScope: Major private Nigerian scheduled carrier of the 1990s and 2000s that operated domestic trunk services, West African coastal network flights, and Boeing 767-200ER services to London Heathrow.
airlines.statusContext: Ceased operations in October 2009: evolved out of Bellview Travels in Lagos in 1992, began scheduled domestic DC-9 passenger services in 1993, expanded across West Africa and to London, and shut down in late 2009 following fleet grounding and IATA Billing and Settlement Plan (BSP) suspension.

airlines.name: ADC Airlines
airlines.iataHistoricalNote: Historical IATA designator Z7 held during scheduled operations in the 1990s and 2000s.
airlines.serviceScope: Pioneer pilot-founded private Nigerian scheduled carrier that operated Boeing 737-200 and DC-9 flights connecting Lagos, Abuja, Calabar, Port Harcourt, Sokoto, Yola, and West African capitals.
airlines.statusContext: Ceased operations in 2006–2007: Aviation Development Company opened in December 1984, commenced ADC Airlines flight operations on 1 January 1991, listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange in 1994, had its licence suspended following the October 2006 Flight 053 accident near Abuja, and did not re-register under the April 2007 NCAA recapitalisation deadline.

airlines.name: Okada Air
airlines.iataHistoricalNote: Historical IATA designator 9H held 1983–1997 (subsequently reassigned globally by IATA).
airlines.serviceScope: Nigeria's trailblazing private domestic passenger and charter airline of the 1980s and 1990s, operating a large fleet of BAC One-Eleven and Boeing 727 jets from Benin Airport across nine Nigerian cities.
airlines.statusContext: Ceased operations in 1997: founded in 1983 by Chief Gabriel Igbinedion in Benin City, commenced flights in September 1983, won scheduled domestic and international route rights in the early 1990s after air deregulation, and wound down operations in 1997.

airlines.name: Sosoliso Airlines
airlines.serviceScope: Scheduled domestic passenger airline linking Lagos and Abuja with South-East and South-South commercial centres at Enugu, Port Harcourt, and Owerri using McDonnell Douglas DC-9 and MD-81/82 aircraft.
airlines.statusContext: Ceased operations in April 2007: incorporated in 1994 (originally headquartered at Enugu Airport before relocating its head office to Ikeja, Lagos) and commenced scheduled flights in July 2000; grounded when it did not meet the Federal Government's 30 April 2007 airline recapitalisation deadline.

airlines.name: Chanchangi Airlines
airlines.iataHistoricalNote: Historical IATA designator 5B held 1997–2012 (subsequently reassigned globally by IATA).
airlines.serviceScope: Privately owned Kaduna-headquartered domestic carrier that operated high-frequency Boeing 727-200 and Boeing 737 passenger shuttles between Kaduna, Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, and Owerri.
airlines.statusContext: Ceased scheduled operations in 2012: incorporated on 5 January 1994 by Alhaji Ahmadu Chanchangi and launched commercial flights on 2 May 1997, winning multiple FAAN Domestic Airline of the Year awards before fleet attrition led to intermittent NCAA groundings between 2010 and final closure in 2012.

airlines.name: First Nation Airways
airlines.serviceScope: Lagos-headquartered domestic trunk passenger carrier that operated Airbus A320 and Airbus A319 aircraft between Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt.
